b: Hotone built the Voclas as a vocal processor, yet the feature that earns it a spot on a guitar channel is the instrument input on the back. Plug a guitar in beside the mic and your chords can steer up to three harmony voices or shape the vocoder, which gives players who never step up to sing a reason to look twice.

Tom Butwin approaches the floor unit as a singer first. Its 62 dB analog preamp supplies 48V phantom power, so his favorite Shure SM86 condenser stayed in the chain. From there the vocal side covers compression, EQ, delay, reverb, and AT-Tune pitch correction that can stay subtle or push into the hard, stepped sound of modern pop. Hotone credits a neural network engine with keeping latency low enough for live correction and harmony, and Tom reports no lag he could hear. Harmonies can follow your guitar chords, a MIDI keyboard, or Hotone’s AI analysis of your vocal line. The same guitar connection works the vocoder and talkbox effects, so your mouth can shape a solo without a plastic tube taped to the mic stand.

There’s also a separate guitar chain with clean, overdrive, and acoustic simulations, a stereo looper with 90 seconds of recording time, a tuner, a touchscreen, and three footswitches for presets, effect toggles, and a talk mode for addressing the crowd dry. As Tom puts it, you could “show up with this and nothing else.
